findings.scope: Scope is correctly limited and stated in Section 5 of the proof file: (i) leading order only, i.e. the limit q to infinity at fixed D and fixed finite data; a deficit that vanishes with q is not excluded and [161] does not control the sign of the o(1) term; (ii) only kernels of the form (3.6) with the pairwise sign-model limit; other kernels, other limit regimes, or limits with terms beyond pairwise parity (e.g. faces with more than three active incidences, where RL(H) is pure assumption) are outside the admissible class; (iii) the barrier applies to every girth-six pattern, inside C_2 as well as outside; the checkpoint attaches it to the outside-C_2 premise because that is the transfer target. The 'barrier' is method-relative, as the strategy study acknowledges, and its evidential weight for the claim is modest; the checkpoint does not overstate it. The next_hypothesis follows from the barrier only in the weak sense that the identified class is excluded.
findings.statement: The checkpoint is an obstruction milestone, not a proof or disproof of the claim (Sidorenko's inequality for girth-six bipartite patterns outside C_2). What is actually established, in proof file ac528fd0...: (Lemma O(a)) for any finite bipartite H with parts I,J and no 4-cycle, the pairwise sign model M_H(B,xi)=E_eta prod_j prod_{{i,k} subset N_B(j)} (1+c_0 eta_{ik} xi_ij xi_kj) equals 1 for every active set B, sign choice xi and c_0 in {1,-1}; (Lemma O(b)) if H has a 4-cycle, M_H takes the values 0 and 2; (Corollary O') under the named assumption RL(H) (the analogue of [161] Lemma 3.1 for H), for every finite choice of type sets, priors, coordinate set and activation laws in the form of [161] Eq. (3.6), lim_q t_{I,J}(W_q)=lim_q t_{I,J}(W_q^T)=1 and lim_q t(H,V_q)=1=(E V_q)^{e(H)} for the symmetrized kernel V_q of [161] Prop. 3.5. I checked each step against the supplied full text of [161]: the independence argument in O(a) is correct (two faces both containing i,k would form i-j-k-j'-i, a 4-cycle, so each eta_P appears in at most one factor and averages it to 1 since E eta_P=0); the 4-cycle computation in O(b) gives 1+ab; the coordinate regrouping in O' (exchange of finite expectations, independence of matrix coordinates given types and activations, uniform o(1) from RL(H), boundedness of M_H, finite average) matches the proof of [161] Lemma 3.2; the identity t(H,V_q)=t_{I,J}(W_q)t_{I,J}(W_q^T) uses only bipartiteness, as in [161] Prop. 3.5; E W_q=1 for all q is stated after (3.6) in [161]. One minor notational slip: in the transpose paragraph of O' the differences are written Y_i^k - X_j^k whereas the kernel W_q^T(y_i,x_j)=W_q(x_j,y_i) produces X_j^k - Y_i^k; this is harmless because RL(H) is assumed for both orientations and Lemma O(a) holds for every sign choice and c_0, so the limit 1 is unaffected. Non-blocking. The conclusion is correctly stated by the checkpoint: the leading-order transfer of [161]'s construction cannot yield a counterexample on any girth-six pattern (inside or outside C_2); the claim itself is neither proved nor refuted and no obligation or route status changes.
